## At a glance
::: {.summary-grid}
Question
:   Do nine ability tests measure three distinct factors?

Data
:   Holzinger & Swineford (1939) · 301 students

Methods
:   Three-factor CFA, ML estimation in Mplus

Finding
:   One sentence on fit and loadings.
:::
:::

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(MplusAutomation)   # runs Mplus and reads its output
library(lavaan)            # only for the example data
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

dir.create("mplus", showWarnings = FALSE)
hs <- HolzingerSwineford1939[, paste0("x", 1:9)]
```
:::


## Mplus model

The `mplusObject()` holds the exact Mplus syntax, so readers see the model as
they would write it in an `.inp` file.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cfa <- mplusObject(
  TITLE    = "Three-factor CFA;",
  ANALYSIS = "ESTIMATOR = ML;",
  MODEL    = "
    visual  BY x1 x2 x3;
    textual BY x4 x5 x6;
    speed   BY x7 x8 x9;",
  OUTPUT   = "STDYX MODINDICES(10);",
  rdata    = hs
)

# Requires a licensed Mplus on the machine that renders this page.
fit <- mplusModeler(cfa, modelout = "mplus/cfa.inp", run = 1L)
```
:::


## Model fit


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit$results$summaries |>
  select(ChiSqM_Value, ChiSqM_DF, CFI, TLI, RMSEA_Estimate, SRMR) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Global fit")
```
:::


## Visualization


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit$results$parameters$stdyx.standardized |>
  filter(grepl("\\.BY$", paramHeader)) |>
  mutate(factor = sub("\\.BY$", "", paramHeader),
         lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se) |>
  ggplot(aes(est, reorder(param, est), colour = factor)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi)) +
  facet_grid(factor ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Standardized loading", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::
